prerequisites: Basic knowledge of mechanics and electromagnetism.
Basic knowledge of mathematical analysis and geometry.

learning_outcomes.text: To provide students the elements to understand some aspects of wave phenomena, electromagnetism, quantum physics, statistical methods, and their applications.

syllabus_topics: Vibrating string, d'Alembert equation, Fourier analysis, sound waves, electromagnetic waves, electromagnetic spectrum.
Harmonic oscillator, resonance, quality factor, tuning circuits, linewidth.
Photon polarization, spin1/2 and Stern Gerlach experiments, two-level atomic systems, quantum dots.
Representation of a two-level system on Bloch sphere.
Equation of motion for Bloch vector.
The second quantum revolution; Quantum technologies; quantum manifesto and quantum flagship.
Measurements in physics and measurement instruments
Methods for statistical data analysis: probability and random variables, probability density functions, expectation values, statistical error propagation.
Examples of probability density functions: binomial, Poisson, uniform, exponential, Gaussian, chi squared.
Parameter estimation and the method of maximum likelihood
Measurements in quantum mechanics: review of basic concepts; precise and imprecise measurements in quantum mechanics; state preparation via measurement.
assessment_rules: The final grade is a single score from 0 to 30, potentially with Honors. A score of 18-22 indicates elementary knowledge with some errors. A score of 26-28 indicates a solid theoretical understanding and problem-solving ability. Honors (Laude) is awarded for work distinguished by brilliance and originality.
